dual_purpose_note: This single JSON file governs TWO distinct things, kept separate in every section below via a 'scope' tag: (1) 'build_pipeline' = the LangGraph/orchestration harness executing THIS SDLC pipeline that builds LordCode; (2) 'product_design' = the harness LordCode itself ships to end users. They share the same mathematical machinery (same skills, same formulas) but are configured with different, independently-calibrated numbers because they run different workloads.

math_delegation.note: No live math-agent invocation channel exists in this standalone dispatch (only claude/Explore/general-purpose/Plan/statusline-setup agent types are spawnable here). Every number below is a DIRECT APPLICATION of an already-derived, cited skill formula (M1-M6 of the six mandatory skills) — never an improvised derivation. Each result below carries its skill+section citation. Formal re-derivation, confidence intervals, and empirical recalibration from real telemetry remain harness-mathematics-expert's job once that agent is reachable in a live pipeline run.

stop-condition-budget-control-core M2/M3: Cost_replay(T) = c*T(T+1)/2 = Theta(T^2); theta* ~= rho*T; T_min = sqrt(2*C_s/(rho*c))
retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core M1: delay(n) = min(cap, base*b^n), n* = ceil(log_b(cap/base))
retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core M2: full jitter delay(n) = U(0,D(n))
retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core M5: binomial false-trip tail, worked at theta=0.5,N=20,r0=0.10 -> P(false trip)~=1.3e-9
tool-call-mediation-core M4: p* = c_a / (d * L_h)  (HITL expected-loss threshold)
tool-call-mediation-core M2: P(correct) ~= 1/(k+1) for k confusable near-duplicate tools
agent-routing-dispatch-policy-core M4: parallel iff no directed path in decomposition DAG; Kahn topological sort O(|V|+|E|); critical-path makespan lower bound
agent-routing-dispatch-policy-core M5: M/M/c stability rho = lambda/(c*mu) < 1, Erlang-C P_wait

loop_lifecycle.scope: both (identical structure; different T_max per class, see stop_predicate.t_max_by_class)
loop_lifecycle.cycle: LLM call -> inspect response -> tool dispatch (if any) -> result fed back -> continue-or-stop
loop_lifecycle.boundary_invariant: the model owns pi (WHICH action/tool/args to propose or final answer); the harness owns E (validation, dispatch, budgeting, continue-or-stop). The harness never lets the model's own text substitute for a stop or approval decision (tool-call-mediation-core Section 2.3).

finishReason_taxonomy.citation: agent-loop-lifecycle-core Section 3.2 + stop-condition-budget-control-core Section 2.2, extended with an abort_reason sub-field to satisfy PRD AC-FR-HRN-003

abort_reason_subfield.rationale: AC-FR-HRN-003 requires a T_max stop to be logged as distinct from a budget-guard stop. The base 4-value taxonomy collapses both into 'aborted' (stop-condition-budget-control-core Section 2.2 table). abort_reason is the disambiguating field the audit log actually needs; it must never be omitted on an aborted run.

finishReason_taxonomy.hard_rule: an aborted result MUST NEVER be reported as a stop result (agent-loop-lifecycle-core Section 3.3, 'a correctness bug'). The harness recovers only the LAST available response on abort, and the audit trail must say so.

order: stopWhen (-> aborted:stopWhen, or graceful per predicate intent)
stop_precedence.why_this_order: a task that completes on its own final allowed turn must be reported as stop, never as an abort just because the turn cap also tripped that same turn.

stop_predicate.formula: STOP(s_t, t, tokens_t) = isFinal(a_t) OR (t >= T_max) OR (tokens_t >= B) OR stopWhen(s_t)
stop_predicate.liveness_guarantee: T_max is the ONLY unconditional termination guarantee (M2's monotone-variant proof: t increments by exactly 1 per turn, so t>=T_max fires by turn T_max regardless of model behaviour). isFinal alone gives NO termination guarantee — never rely on the model eventually stopping.

t_max_by_class.note: A single global T_max is an anti-pattern (agent-loop-lifecycle-core Anti-Patterns: 'ignoring the fitted per-turn continuation probability p_c for the specific task class'). LordCode's specialist roster is heterogeneous, so T_max is sized per invocation class from a provisional per-turn stop probability p. ALL p values below are provisional placeholders pending real per-class telemetry from Phase H (>=5 replays); recalibrate before ACTING mode.

rate_limit.mechanism: token bucket (C, r) per provider connection
rate_limit.recovery: wait for refill — never a hard stop

budget_limit.mechanism: cumulative counter vs B, per agent-loop invocation
budget_limit.governs: total spend for that invocation (stock axis, W(T) <= B)
budget_limit.recovery: none within the invocation — hard stop, finishReason=aborted, abort_reason=budget

two_orthogonal_levers.orthogonality_rule: both are enforced independently; satisfying one gives no guarantee about the other, especially under multi-provider fan-out where several invocations draw on the same provider's rate-limit headroom simultaneously.

context_replay_cost_model.provisional_note: c=2000 is an illustrative placeholder informed by the 20,000-32,000 token Context Budget fields already used for individual specialist dispatches in docs/orchestration_prompt.md, divided across an assumed multi-turn footprint. MUST be replaced with go-systems-engineer's measured harness telemetry (mean tokens added per turn: one tool-call request + one tool-result) before ACTING mode.

compaction_policy.T_min_interpretation: compaction never pays for itself below ~2.3 remaining turns — do not compact short invocations (class R at T_max=15 still comfortably clears this; all three classes benefit from compaction).

budget_guard_B_per_invocation.citation: stop-condition-budget-control-core M2/M3 (post-compaction total = R_full(theta*) + C_s + R_red(theta*))
budget_guard_B_per_invocation.derivation_note: B is set with headroom above the expected post-compaction total cost per class, computed at the class's own T_max as a worst-case ceiling (most runs stop far earlier at their natural E[T]=1/p, per M5 of agent-loop-lifecycle-core).
budget_guard_B_per_invocation.hard_rule: B is enforced independent of and in addition to the post-run cost DISPLAY (PRD FR-COR-006) — B is a mandatory stop disjunct, never optional, never user-configurable to 'unlimited' (PRD constraint (d): no spend ceilings/approval prompts is about NOT gating the user's SPEND CHOICE up front; it is not a licence to remove the harness's own runaway-safety invariant).

retryable_conditions: provider transient (e.g. Anthropic overloaded_error, OpenAI server_error)

jitter.rationale: maximum decorrelation across concurrent invocations hitting the same provider (retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core M2) — mandatory on every backoff, never a bare deterministic schedule.

expected_outcome_at_k3.citation: retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core M3 worked example, reused as LordCode's provisional calibration point

retry_policy.retry_budget_whole_invocation: no more than 10% of an invocation's total tool/provider calls may be retries; a retry consumes a turn-equivalent and is charged against the same T_max/B stop-predicate bound as any other turn (retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core Section 1.3).
retry_policy.distinctness_rule: retry (this section) is NEVER conflated with circuit-breaking (next section) or with SC.1-3 self-correction (see retry_hierarchy).

circuit_breaker_policy.scope: product_design (per-provider execution breaker) — the build_pipeline uses the SAME structure against whichever provider/model executes each dispatched agent's calls
circuit_breaker_policy.granularity: ONE breaker PER CONFIGURED PROVIDER, never a single global breaker (PRD FR-RTG-004, orchestration_prompt.md CONSTRAINTS repeated verbatim). This is the harness's own EXECUTION breaker and is a distinct instance from the router's routing-CONFIDENCE breaker (see distinct_from_router_breaker below) — both exist, for different consumers.

false_trip_check.citation: retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core M5 worked example at theta=0.5, N=20, r0=0.10 — directly reused since LordCode's provisional baseline matches the skill's own worked calibration point.

circuit_breaker_policy.cooldown_backoff: cooldown itself doubles on consecutive trips, cap 300s (retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core Section 4.2)
circuit_breaker_policy.distinct_from_router_breaker: the multi-model-router-architect's confidence-gate breaker (orchestration_prompt.md line ~272: 50% failure / 60s window / 30s half-open) scores provider HEALTH as an input to the router's argmax model-selection decision (D23, WHICH model). This harness breaker (D50) instead wraps the LIVE call the harness is currently executing for an already-routed invocation. When THIS breaker trips OPEN, the harness does not re-score — it emits the 'explicit circuit-breaker fallback' event named in Alignment 1, and the router re-routes the NEXT invocation via its own argmax over remaining CLOSED-breaker configured providers. The two breakers are configured independently and must not be merged into one.
circuit_breaker_policy.fail_fast_rule: no retries are attempted while a provider's breaker is OPEN — retrying through an open breaker defeats the blast-radius bound (retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core M6).

retry_hierarchy.scope: both — this is the seam that resolves Alignment 6, see alignment_6_position below

tiers.name: tool/provider call retry
tiers.scope_of_recovery: one HTTP/tool call, k<=3 attempts, seconds

tiers.name: circuit breaker
tiers.scope_of_recovery: one provider, systemic failure, seconds-to-minutes, fails fast + triggers router fallback

tiers.name: SC.1-3 self-correction
tiers.owner: SDLC pipeline engine (D39), NOT the harness — the harness only supplies the signal (finishReason, abort_reason, retry/breaker counts) that root-cause-analysis-agent consumes
tiers.scope_of_recovery: one PHASE GATE, <=3 iterations then human escalation, minutes-to-hours

retry_hierarchy.hard_rule: never conflate tiers. A tier-1 retry exhausting its cap does not by itself constitute an SC.1 event — it surfaces as a tool-result observation the MODEL may react to (tool-call-mediation-core Section 4.3); only a GATE-LEVEL failure (the phase's evaluator returns REJECT/FAIL) triggers SC.1-3.

tool_mediation.soundness_invariant: dispatched set D subset-of V^-1(1) — malformed arguments are rejected before dispatch, never coerced through a permissive schema (M3).

toolset_size_policy.citation: tool-call-mediation-core Section 5, M2: P(correct) ~= 1/(k+1) for k confusable near-duplicates — empirical <80% accuracy threshold reported near 15-20 tools, flagged as vendor-reported not derived
toolset_size_policy.mitigation: decompose into focused sub-agents rather than overload one agent's toolset; already the library's own convention across its 528 compiled agents.

hitl_approval_threshold.formula: require approval iff p > c_a / (d * L_h)

applied_to_lordcode_dangerous_actions.action_class: file deletion outside PROJECT_PATH, or any recursive delete
applied_to_lordcode_dangerous_actions.reasoning: L_h -> very large (irrecoverable data loss, possible credential-file destruction); p* collapses toward 0 regardless of c_a, d.

applied_to_lordcode_dangerous_actions.action_class: git push to a protected branch (main) or any force-push
applied_to_lordcode_dangerous_actions.reasoning: L_h high (irreversible history rewrite, possible secret exposure); a single confirmation (low c_a) is cheap relative to the loss.

applied_to_lordcode_dangerous_actions.action_class: git push to a pipeline-created, non-protected feature/scratch branch (normal Phase G operation)
applied_to_lordcode_dangerous_actions.reasoning: L_h materially lower — the branch is disposable and protected-branch policy already prevents direct main damage; gating this would add friction to the pipeline's own routine Phase G push-and-PR flow with no proportionate risk reduction (tool-call-mediation-core Anti-Pattern: uniform gating regardless of harm severity).

applied_to_lordcode_dangerous_actions.action_class: arbitrary network call to a host outside the three configured provider endpoints or the daemon's own declared integrations
applied_to_lordcode_dangerous_actions.policy: DENY by default (allowlist-only egress); REQUIRE_APPROVAL to add a host to the allowlist
applied_to_lordcode_dangerous_actions.reasoning: SSRF and credential-exfiltration risk are named CRITICAL in the PRD's Security Risk section; L_h includes cross-user credential leakage on the multi-tenant daemon.

applied_to_lordcode_dangerous_actions.action_class: read-only operations (list/read files, git status/diff/log, read-only provider calls)
applied_to_lordcode_dangerous_actions.reasoning: L_h near 0; gating every read imposes friction with no risk reduction (p* > 1).

score_inputs: capability-DNA fit for the task class
provider_failover.trigger: harness-triggered circuit-breaker fallback (Alignment 1) or a new task — never a mid-execution re-route of an already-dispatched invocation.

decomposition_dag.rule: two subtasks parallelise iff no directed path connects them in the dependency DAG (M4)
decomposition_dag.scheduling: Kahn's topological sort, O(|V|+|E|), level/antichain waves
decomposition_dag.applied_to_lordcode: docs/orchestration_prompt.md's Phase B.1-B.9 already marks explicit parallel groups (e.g. B.2 || B.3); the SDLC engine (D39) owns this decomposition, the harness executes each resulting node's invocation.
decomposition_dag.critical_path_rule: phase gates (Phase 0->1->1.5->...->Ops.5) are hard sequential barriers; makespan is lower-bounded by the SUM of each phase's own critical path, not reducible by adding daemon workers beyond each phase's own antichain width — see forty_to_eighty_invocation_analysis.

daemon_worker_pool_sizing.stability_condition: rho = lambda / (c * mu) < 1  =>  c > lambda / mu

worked_illustrative_example.derivation_of_mu: E[T]_class_I = 1/p = 1/0.15 = 6.67 turns; W = E[T]*(l_LLM + l_tool) = 6.67*(3s+1s) = 26.7s; mu = 1/W = 0.0375 invocations/sec/worker
worked_illustrative_example.note: lambda and per-turn latencies (l_LLM, l_tool) are PLACEHOLDERS. site-reliability-engineer (Ops.2) must replace with measured RED-dashboard values before this number is used for real capacity planning; this is a sizing METHODOLOGY handoff, not a provisioned value.

forty_to_eighty_invocation_analysis.scope: product_design — this is the direct answer to 'what does 40-80+ invocations per requirement do to Little's Law, replay cost, and failure semantics'

littles_law_across_pipeline.claim: L_pipeline (mean invocations in flight for one requirement) is NOT 40-80 simultaneously — it equals the ANTICHAIN WIDTH at each DAG wave, which the SDLC engine's decomposition already keeps small (e.g. Phase F.2/F.3/F.4 run 2-3 agents in parallel each, not all 40-80 at once). Wall-clock time for one requirement is dominated by the SEQUENTIAL SUM of phase-gate critical paths, not by daemon concurrency — matching agent-routing-dispatch-policy-core M4's critical-path lower bound.
littles_law_across_pipeline.consequence: provisioning the daemon for 'one requirement = 80 concurrent workers' over-provisions badly; the correct sizing input is the MAX antichain width across all phases (typically single digits) times the number of CONCURRENT REQUIREMENTS the daemon serves multi-tenant, which is the lambda used in daemon_worker_pool_sizing above.

context_replay_cost_across_the_whole_run.wrong_model: treating the whole 40-80-invocation run as ONE loop of T=(sum of all invocations' turns) and applying Cost_replay(T)=c*T(T+1)/2 to that combined T — this would be catastrophically over-quadratic and is explicitly the anti-pattern stop-condition-budget-control-core warns against ('budgeting a long-running loop's cost as linear... or the wrong horizon').
context_replay_cost_across_the_whole_run.correct_model: each of the N=40-80 invocations gets an ISOLATED, freshly-bounded context per invocation (context-engineering-agent's DPDP-Section-4 per-story context isolation, already a named library convention for daemon per-user isolation under ADR-6). The quadratic Theta(T_i^2) cost RESETS per invocation. Total pipeline replay cost is therefore Sigma_{i=1}^{N} Cost_replay(T_i) = O(N * T_max^2) at worst case (linear in invocation count, quadratic only within each bounded invocation) — never O((N*T_max)^2).
context_replay_cost_across_the_whole_run.worst_case_illustrative: N=80, all class_I, all hit T_max=30: 80 * 589800 (post-compaction total, see budget_guard_B_per_invocation derivation) ~= 47.2M tokens — an explicit upper bound, not an expectation.
context_replay_cost_across_the_whole_run.realistic_expected_illustrative: using E[T]=1/p=6.67 turns for class_I instead of the T_max worst case: per-invocation expected replay ~= c*E[T]*(E[T]+1)/2 = 2000*6.67*7.67/2 ~= 51,100 tokens; across N=80 ~= 4.09M tokens. This expected figure, itemised per phase, is the number FR-COR-006's post-run cost display should approximate — it is large but BOUNDED, consistent with the product's accepted-not-gated cost stance.

failure_semantics_invocation_57_of_80.question: if invocation #57 of 80 fails, what happens to the 56 before it?
failure_semantics_invocation_57_of_80.answer: they are NOT rolled back. PRD FR-SDL-004 mandates pipeline state persisted across process invocations; checkpointing is PER-PHASE-GATE, not per-invocation-transaction. A completed invocation whose phase's gate has already recorded PASS is a durable checkpoint (idempotent) and stays valid regardless of a later invocation's failure.
failure_semantics_invocation_57_of_80.granularity_of_retry: invocation #57 itself is retried individually first, at tool/provider-call granularity (retry_policy, tier 1) — this is far cheaper than any phase-level action and is tried first.
failure_semantics_invocation_57_of_80.gate_atomicity: if #57 is a member of an in-flight ANTICHAIN (parallel group) whose phase gate has not yet been evaluated, the gate evaluation is atomic PER PHASE: the phase cannot pass until every required member of that antichain reports. Sibling invocations in the same antichain that already completed are held (bounded by their own T_max/B, which prevents an indefinite stall) pending #57's outcome — they are not discarded, and re-running them is unnecessary once #57 resolves.
failure_semantics_invocation_57_of_80.escalation_path: if #57 exhausts its tier-1 retry cap and the phase's gate evaluator records REJECT/FAIL, that is an SC.1 event (tier 3, owned by the SDLC engine): root-cause-analysis-agent runs, retries the FAILING STEP up to 3 total SC iterations (PRD FR-SDL-002/AC-FR-SDL-002), with RE_ROUTE to Phase 1 on an architecture_gap cause or Phase 0 on a wrong_design_assumption cause. On a 4th consecutive failure, escalate to a human reviewer with the phase's full state preserved (AC-FR-SDL-002) — nothing ABOVE the current phase boundary is lost or re-run.
failure_semantics_invocation_57_of_80.net_answer: the 56 prior invocations survive as durable, gate-checkpointed artifacts; only invocation 57 (and any not-yet-started transitive dependents of it in the DAG) are actually at risk, and even that risk is bounded by three nested, increasingly coarse-grained recovery tiers before a human is ever paged.

alignment_6_position.question: does LordCode ship ONE merged engine, or TWO layered engines (harness = lower layer executing one invocation; SDLC engine = upper layer sequencing phases and evaluating gates, a CLIENT of the harness)?
alignment_6_position.position: TWO layered engines — the harness is the LOWER layer, the SDLC engine is the UPPER layer and a CLIENT of the harness. Argued FOR, not assumed.
reasoning: the same WHAT/HOW split that governs a single agent loop (agent-loop-lifecycle-core Section 2: model decides WHAT, harness mediates HOW) recurs one level up: the SDLC engine decides WHAT sequence of phases/gates/agents constitutes a requirement's pipeline; the harness mediates HOW any ONE of those dispatched agent invocations actually executes (stop conditions, retries, budget, tool mediation). Merging them would blur exactly the boundary Operating Rule 1 forbids blurring.

the retry_hierarchy above is only coherent as three CLEANLY SEPARATED tiers if tier 3 (SC.1-3, gate-level) sits structurally above tiers 1-2 (call retry, circuit breaker) rather than being reimplemented inside the harness — SC.1-3 needs phase-scoped state (which gate, which prior phases passed) that is the SDLC engine's concern, not the harness's per-invocation loop state.

PRD FR-SDL-005 already requires 'which agents run' (SDLC engine) and 'which model each runs on' (router) to be independently overridable — the SAME orthogonality argument (Alignment 7) applies one layer down: 'which agents run in what phase order' (SDLC engine) and 'how one dispatched invocation is executed' (harness) must stay independently overridable too, or overriding a harness parameter (e.g. a provider fallback) would risk silently changing which agents the SDLC engine dispatches — exactly the coupling FR-SDL-005 forbids in the sibling case.

gate-calibration-scoring-core's GACS auto-approve scoring is explicitly a GATE-EVALUATOR concern (Phase 1.5 and Phase 5 pilots only) — it belongs to the SDLC engine's gate-evaluation logic, consuming S_RS/S_con from OTHER domains and S_loss's harm-probability generalisation from THIS domain's M4, but the decision itself (auto-approve vs escalate a PHASE gate) is upper-layer business, not something the harness's own stop predicate should absorb.

operationally: this makes B.1 (SDLC pipeline engine) and B.3 (harness/agent-loop runtime) genuinely parallelisable Phase-B work items (as orchestration_prompt.md's STEP 10 already marks them, 'B.2 parallel with B.3'), because a clean client/server layering lets them be built and tested independently against a stable interface, rather than as one entangled module that cannot be parallel-developed.
alignment_6_position.interface_the_HLD_must_specify: the exact call the SDLC engine makes to dispatch one agent invocation through the harness (inputs: agent id, router-selected provider/model per Alignment 1, tool-set, T_max class, budget B; outputs: finishReason, abort_reason if any, tool-call trace for replay, cost). This is the seam consensus-agent's Phase-2 gate treats as mandatory (docs/orchestration_prompt.md line ~1512: 'An HLD that leaves this ambiguous is REJECTED').
alignment_6_position.caveat: this is harness-engineering-architect's INPUT to solution-architect, per agent.md and Alignment 6's own text ('solution-architect owns the verdict, you supply the input') — it is not a final architectural decision. If Phase 1 disagrees, it must record why in an ADR.
